title: Best Ebook Formats: EPUB vs PDF vs MOBI
excerpt: EPUB, PDF, and MOBI all have different strengths. Choosing the wrong format for the wrong platform means formatting problems and potential rejections. Here's exactly which format to use and when.
meta_title: EPUB vs PDF vs MOBI: Which Ebook Format Should You Use? | BookKraft AI
meta_description: Choosing between EPUB, PDF, and MOBI for your ebook? This guide explains the real differences, which platforms accept which format, and which one to publish in for best results.
html:
When you're ready to publish your ebook, the first decision isn't about platforms or pricing — it's about format. EPUB, PDF, and MOBI are the three formats you'll encounter most often, and they behave very differently depending on where and how they're read.

Choosing the wrong format means readers get a poor experience, platforms reject your file, or your formatting breaks on certain devices. Here's what each format actually does and when to use it.

EPUB: The Industry Standard

EPUB is the format that every major ebook platform except Amazon accepts. Apple Books, Kobo, Google Play Books, Barnes & Noble, Draft2Digital, IngramSpark — all of them use EPUB as their primary format.

EPUB is a reflowable format. Text wraps to fit whatever screen size the reader is using. If a reader makes the text larger, paragraphs reflow. If they switch from a phone to a tablet, the layout adjusts. The reading experience adapts to the device rather than being locked to a specific layout.

EPUB 3.0 is the current version of the standard. It supports HTML5, CSS3, embedded fonts, audio, video, and accessibility features. EPUB 2.0 still works on most platforms but is the older version and has fewer capabilities.

Use EPUB when: You're publishing anywhere other than Amazon, or when you're publishing wide across multiple platforms. EPUB is also the right choice if you want the cleanest reading experience on e-readers and mobile devices.

Before uploading your EPUB anywhere, run it through the EPUB Validator to catch structural errors that would get it rejected. Different platforms have different tolerance levels — what KDP accepts, Apple Books may reject.

MOBI: The Old Kindle Format

MOBI is Amazon's legacy format. Older Kindle devices use MOBI, and it's derived from an even older format called PalmDOC. If you've ever seen a .mobi file, it was almost certainly meant for Kindle.

Amazon has been phasing MOBI out for years. KDP Direct Publishing stopped accepting MOBI uploads in 2022. The current Kindle publishing format is KFX (Kindle Format 10), which KDP generates internally from your EPUB upload.

You'll still encounter MOBI in a few places: older Kindle device sideloading, some personal libraries, and some book distribution networks that haven't updated to EPUB. But for new publishing, MOBI is not the format you should be creating or submitting.

Use MOBI when: You have a specific reason to sideload a file to an older Kindle device for personal use. For commercial publishing, don't use MOBI — submit EPUB to KDP instead.

PDF: Fixed Layout for Print-Like Documents

PDF is not a reflowable ebook format — it's a fixed-layout document format. Every element on every page is positioned at a specific coordinate. The text doesn't reflow when the font size changes. The layout doesn't adapt to screen size.

This makes PDF excellent for documents that need to look the same everywhere: textbooks, cookbooks, technical manuals, children's picture books, and print-to-digital conversions where layout matters. But for standard trade novels and non-fiction books, PDF is a poor choice.

Reading a PDF novel on a phone means zooming in to read, then scrolling horizontally to get to the end of each line. It's uncomfortable and that's why most readers prefer EPUB for prose.

Some platforms accept PDF, but they don't use it the same way they use EPUB. KDP accepts PDF for print book formatting (the print interior), not for ebook distribution. Draft2Digital does not accept PDF for ebook distribution.

Use PDF when: You're submitting a print book interior to KDP or IngramSpark, or when you're publishing a heavily illustrated book where precise layout control matters more than device adaptability.

Which Format Should You Publish In?

For most authors publishing trade books (novels, memoirs, business books, narrative non-fiction), the answer is clear:

  • For KDP: Upload EPUB. KDP converts it to Kindle's internal format.
  • For Apple Books: Upload EPUB 3.0. Apple is strict about EPUB quality — validate before uploading.
  • For Kobo, Google Play, B&N: Upload EPUB.
  • For IngramSpark: Upload EPUB for ebook distribution, PDF for print.
  • For Draft2Digital: Upload EPUB or your manuscript (they convert it for you).

If you're publishing in multiple places, create one high-quality EPUB and use it everywhere. Don't maintain separate files for each platform — it's unnecessary and creates more opportunities for version inconsistencies.

Converting Between Formats

If you have a manuscript and need an EPUB, the Full Manuscript Mode converts your .docx or .txt directly to valid EPUB 3.0 in one step — with chapter detection, clean HTML output, and proper metadata structure.

If you have a Word document with formatting issues that need cleaning before conversion, run it through the Word Cleanup Checker first. It identifies double spaces, straight quotes, stacked blank paragraphs, and other common Word-to-EPUB conversion problems before they become EPUB errors.

Avoid converting from PDF to EPUB when possible. PDF-to-EPUB conversion produces poor results — the fixed layout structure of PDF doesn't translate cleanly to reflowable EPUB, and you usually get garbled text, broken paragraphs, and lost formatting.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Amazon KDP still accept MOBI files?

No. KDP stopped accepting MOBI uploads in 2022. Submit EPUB to KDP — they convert it to their internal Kindle format automatically.

Can I use the same EPUB file for every platform?

Yes, with caveats. A well-formed EPUB 3.0 file works across all major platforms. The caveat is that different platforms have different validation strictness. An EPUB that passes KDP may fail Apple Books. Validate your EPUB thoroughly before submitting to any platform.

What's the difference between EPUB 2.0 and EPUB 3.0?

EPUB 3.0 is the current standard and supports HTML5, CSS3, MathML, embedded audio and video, and enhanced accessibility features. EPUB 2.0 is still widely supported but is the older version. If you're creating a new EPUB, use EPUB 3.0.

Is PDF acceptable for ebook readers?

Technical yes, practical no — for prose books. PDF works well for highly designed books (cookbooks, children's books, technical manuals) where layout matters more than device adaptability. For novels and standard non-fiction, PDF gives readers a worse experience than EPUB on phone and e-reader screens.

How do I know if my EPUB is good quality?

Run it through the BookKraft AI EPUB Validator. It checks structure, HTML validity, OPF manifest, TOC, image references, and CSS compliance — the same checks that publishing platforms use. If it passes validator, it's ready to upload.
